rows.grounds: compound of kapaṭeśvara (name/epithet) and sampūjyā (to be worshipped, adored); feminine singular epithet of the goddess
compound of kapaṭeśvara (name/epithet) and rūpiṇī (having the form of); feminine singular epithet of the goddess

items.question: In what modes of relation is the goddess connected to Kapaṭeśvara?
premises: The goddess is described as worshipped by Kapaṭeśvara.
The goddess is described as having the form of Kapaṭeśvara.
Both epithets present Kapaṭeśvara as central to her identity.
items.inference: The goddess stands in relation to Kapaṭeśvara both as the object of his worship and as one who embodies his form.
uncertainties: kapaṭeśvara is treated as a proper name or epithet without further specification in this verse.
items.plain_english: She is worshipped by Kapaṭeśvara and takes the form of Kapaṭeśvara.
